title: OneDrive sync app: policy to exclude folders by name from upload on Windows and Mac
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents the Windows and Mac controls, their opt-in default and the limits on existing synced content. The rollout dates match the release notes, and the briefing correctly reports their disagreement with the roadmap status.

claims.claim: The Windows folder exclusion control is in Group Policy Management Editor under Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > OneDrive > Exclude specific kinds of folders from being uploaded.
claims.quote: Under Computer Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\OneDrive, navigate to Computer Configuration > Policies. ... Exclude specific kinds of folders from being uploaded

claims.claim: Windows folder exclusions are a list of folder-name strings under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive\EnableODIgnoreFolderListFromGPO.
claims.quote: Enabling this policy creates a list of strings under the following path: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive\EnableODIgnoreFolderListFromGPO

claims.claim: Intune deploys the Mac folder preference through Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > macOS > Templates > Preference file > Configuration settings > Property list file.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy. ... Platform: Select macOS ... Profile type: Select Templates > Preference file. ... In Configuration settings ... Property list file

claims.where: controls[1].api; What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The standalone Mac edition uses the EnableODIgnoreFolders array of folder-name strings in /Library/Preferences/com.microsoft.OneDrive.plist.
claims.quote:
.plist location | /Library/Preferences/com.microsoft.OneDrive.plist ... <key>EnableODIgnoreFolders</key>
<array>
<string>(Folder name such as PowerShell)</string>
</array>

claims.claim: The Windows user-exclusion control is in Group Policy Management Editor under Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > OneDrive > Prevent users at your organization from changing the default ignored extension and folder lists.
claims.quote: Under Computer Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\OneDrive ... Prevent users at your organization from changing the default ignored extension and folder lists

claims.claim: Setting the Windows DisableChangesToODIgnoreList DWORD to 1 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive prevents user changes to exclusions.
claims.quote: Enabling this policy sets the following registry key value to 1: [HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive]"DisableChangesToODIgnoreList"=dword:00000001

claims.claim: Intune deploys the Mac user-exclusion preference through Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > macOS > Templates > Preference file > Configuration settings > Property list file.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy. ... Platform: Select macOS ... Profile type: Select Templates > Preference file. ... In Configuration settings ... Property list file

claims.claim: Setting DisableChangesToODIgnoreList to true in the standalone Mac edition's /Library/Preferences/com.microsoft.OneDrive.plist prevents user changes to exclusions.
claims.quote:
.plist location | /Library/Preferences/com.microsoft.OneDrive.plist ... <key>DisableChangesToODIgnoreList</key>
<true/>

claims.claim: The roadmap says users will see excluded folders in the sync configuration in OneDrive Advanced Settings.

claims.claim: An existing Windows file-exclusion setting is Exclude specific kinds of files from being uploaded, identified by EnableODIgnoreListFromGPO.
claims.quote: (EnableODIgnoreListFromGPO) Exclude specific kinds of files from being uploaded

claims.claim: The Mac file-exclusion preference is EnableODIgnore.
claims.quote: EnableODIgnore ... This setting lets you enter keywords to prevent the OneDrive sync app from uploading certain files to OneDrive or SharePoint.

claims.claim: Folder exclusions take complete folder names.
claims.quote: This setting lets you enter complete folder names to prevent the OneDrive sync app (OneDrive.exe) from uploading matching folders to OneDrive or SharePoint.

claims.claim: Folder-name matching is not case-sensitive.
claims.quote: Folder-name matching isn't case-sensitive.

claims.claim: Folder exclusions do not support wildcards.
claims.quote: Wildcards aren't supported.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Enabling the setting prevents the sync app uploading new folders whose names match the administrator's list.
claims.quote: If you enable this setting, the sync app doesn't upload new folders that match the names you specified.

claims.claim: The policy reference says new files created in an existing matching folder are not uploaded.
claims.quote: New files created in an existing matching folder also aren't uploaded.

claims.claim: Skipped folders produce no errors.
claims.quote: No errors appear for the skipped folders

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: New matching folders skipped by the sync app remain in the local OneDrive folder.
claims.quote: No errors appear for the skipped folders, and the folders remain in the local OneDrive folder.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The setting does not retroactively remove a folder or its existing content from OneDrive or SharePoint.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't retroactively remove a folder or its existing content from OneDrive or SharePoint.

claims.claim: Moving files that already sync into an excluded folder is unsupported.
claims.quote: Moving files that are already syncing into an excluded folder isn't supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The folder exclusion setting requires restarting the sync app after it is enabled or changed.
claims.quote: The OneDrive sync app must be restarted after this setting is enabled or changed for the setting to take effect.

claims.claim: Removing an exclusion can cause matching local content to start uploading, and Microsoft advises reviewing that content before removing a rule.
claims.quote: Removing an exclusion can cause matching local content to begin uploading. Review the local content before removing a rule.

claims.claim: The Windows production-ring release notes list folder exclusions in build 26.134.0713.0007 dated July 31, 2026.
claims.quote: Windows Production Ring ... 26.134.0713.0007 (July 31, 2026) ... Exclude specific folders from syncing

claims.claim: The macOS production-ring release notes list folder exclusions in build 26.134.0713.0007 dated July 31, 2026.
claims.quote: macOS Production Ring ... 26.134.0713.0007 (July 31, 2026) ... Exclude specific folders from syncing

claims.claim: The Windows release notes describe folder exclusions as gradually rolling out.
claims.quote: New features gradually rolling out: ... Exclude specific folders from syncing: Administrators can use a new Group Policy setting

claims.claim: The macOS release notes describe folder exclusions as gradually rolling out.
claims.quote: New features gradually rolling out: ... Exclude specific folders from syncing: Administrators can use the EnableODIgnoreFolders managed preference

claims.claim: The release notes say existing synced content is not affected.
claims.quote: Existing synced content is not affected.

claims.claim: Returning a Windows Group Policy setting to Not configured does not modify its registry key or make the change take effect.
claims.quote: If you later change the setting back to Not configured, the corresponding registry key isn't modified, and the change doesn't take effect.

claims.claim: Enabled or Disabled, rather than Not configured, updates a previously configured Group Policy registry setting.
claims.quote: When you enable or disable a setting, the corresponding registry key is updated on computers in your domain. ... After you configure a setting, set it to Enabled or Disabled, going forward.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The installed OneDrive sync app provides administrative template files in its adm folder.
claims.quote: Installing the sync app downloads the .adml and .admx files. ... Browse to %localappdata%\Microsoft\OneDrive\*BuildNumber*\adm\

claims.claim: The OneDrive .admx goes in the domain Central Store and the .adml in its appropriate language subfolder.
claims.quote: Paste the .admx file in your domain's Central Store ... and the .adml file in the appropriate language subfolder, such as en-us.

claims.claim: A OneDrive Group Policy object can be linked to an organisational unit.
claims.quote: Link the GPOs to an Active Directory container (a site, domain, or an organizational unit).

claims.claim: The Windows policy applies to devices within the Group Policy object's scope.
claims.quote: By default, a setting is applied to all user and computer objects within the container to which it's linked, but you can use security filtering to narrow the scope

claims.claim: The preference keys are the same in the standalone and Mac App Store editions.
claims.quote: The keys are the same whether you run the standalone or Mac App Store edition of the sync app.

claims.claim: The standalone preference domain is com.microsoft.OneDrive, while the Mac App Store edition uses com.microsoft.OneDrive-mac and a different .plist.
claims.quote: Domain | com.microsoft.OneDrive | com.microsoft.OneDrive-mac ... However, the .plist file name and domain name are different. When you apply the settings, ensure that you target the appropriate domain

claims.claim: Deploying a preference file through Intune requires the device to be enrolled and MDM managed by Intune.
claims.quote: The device must be enrolled and MDM managed by Intune.

claims.claim: The Intune preference-file instructions require the Policy and Profile Manager built-in role.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Intune admin center with an account that has the Policy and Profile Manager built-in role.
